item.statement: Our theory explains the dense-to-sparse transition seen in McCracken 2025, arising from changing either homogeneity degree or regularization
item.what_to_check: Verify what McCracken actually varies and observes

chk.evidence:
Sources fetched: the arXiv abstract and HTML v1 of 2505.18266, and the NeurIPS 2025 poster page (neurips.cc/virtual/2025/poster/115005). The OpenReview forum zuHs6RHQwT only showed a browser-verification screen.

**The paper:** "Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks" by Gavin McCracken, Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja, Vincent Letourneau, Doina Precup and Jonathan Love, NeurIPS 2025. The refs.bib entry has a nonexistent title and first author ("Andrew McCracken") and must be replaced.

**What McCracken varies and observes:**
- Sec 4.4 / Fig 4 ("Average number of frequencies found in MLPs over moduli 59-66"): "Previous work shows floor(n/2) types of neurons are found ... with 1 hidden layer. We show that adding either depth, or a trainable embedding matrix for inputs, causes the network to transition from learning floor(n/2) types of neurons to much fewer types in Fig. 4."
- App E.4 / Table 5: one-hot ReLU MLPs with 1-4 hidden layers, plus an embedding MLP with 1 hidden layer. Width 1024, lr 7.5e-4, 90% train split, and L2 regularization 1e-5 in every row. Regularization is held fixed.
- All networks are ReLU. The activation or polynomial degree is never varied; quadratic nets are cited only as Gromov's prior theory.
- App G.9.1: "More overparameterized means less frequencies". G.9.2: "Adding depth also means less frequencies are learned".
- Sec 5.1: "While we are the first to point out how to cause a phase transition from O(n) to O(log(n)) learned frequencies (Fig. 4), we don't know why it occurs."

**Degree half: defensible as our reinterpretation.** McCracken's knobs are depth and a trainable embedding. Both raise the homogeneity degree of a ReLU network:
- one-hot, 1 hidden layer: nu=2=b, the dense endpoint (our appendix.tex:283 says this);
- with an embedding or an extra layer: nu>=3 > b=2, the sparse regime.
The sparse count they observe, O(log n), matches our K*=Theta(log p).

**Regularization half: no external support.** McCracken fixes L2 at 1e-5. Morwani et al. 2311.07568 (fetched HTML) do not show a regularization-driven change in frequency count either. Their Fig 4 compares per-neuron sparsity (max power ~0.9 for ReLU+L2 vs ~1 for quadratic+L_{2,3}). Their Fig 7 shows near-uniform coverage of all frequencies for both.

**"Explains" overreaches for ReLU.** Our theorems cover product and power neurons. For ReLU the appendix proves only the b=nu upper bound, and says density of the max-margin ReLU network is "a statement about the bound's maximizer, not a theorem about the network". The deep and embedding ReLU nets McCracken studies are covered by no theorem of ours.

**Searches run:** the paper title with "NeurIPS 2025"; full-text grep of the McCracken HTML for weight decay, quadratic, phase transition, Fig 4, depth, embedding and activation; Morwani HTML checked for L2 vs L_{2,3} frequency counts.

Notes: /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/f3-explains-transition/CHECK.md

recommended_citations.why: Supports the empirical dense-to-sparse transition: Sec 4.4 / Fig 4 shows that adding depth or a trainable embedding moves ReLU MLPs from floor(n/2) to O(log n) frequencies, with L2 fixed at 1e-5 (App E.4 Table 5). Sec 5.1 says 'we don't know why it occurs'. Cite for the transition and for depth/embedding as the knob. Do not cite it for degree or regularization being varied. Venue confirmed via the neurips.cc poster page 115005.

Dense endpoint: Thm 7 says every frequency is used at the max L_{2,3} margin, and Fig 7 shows near-uniform coverage for one-hot 1-layer ReLU+L2 and for quadratic+L_{2,3}. This is consistent with our nu=b=2 ReLU reading. It does NOT show a regularization-induced frequency-count transition (its Fig 4 is about per-neuron sparsity only). Title and authors confirmed from the fetched arXiv HTML; the ICLR 2024 venue was not re-fetched here and comes from the sweep's LIT_ml.md.

chk.recommended_change:
1. Fix refs.bib `mccracken2025`. It should read: title "Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks"; authors Gavin McCracken, Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja, Vincent Létourneau, Doina Precup, Jonathan Love; venue NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2505.18266.

2. Rewrite the last sentence of the abstract (paper.tex:57) so it names the knob McCracken actually turned and does not overclaim "explains". Suggested text: "Further, our theory accounts for the transition from dense to sparse feature counts: raising the homogeneity degree above the regularization exponent, or lowering the exponent below the degree, moves the optimum from all frequencies to Theta(log p) of them. This is consistent with \citet{mccracken2025}, who observe that adding depth or a trainable embedding (each raises the degree of a ReLU network) moves networks from floor(p/2) to O(log p) frequencies."

3. intro.tex:6: replace "as the degree of the network changes \citep{mccracken2025}" with "when depth or a trainable embedding is added \citep{mccracken2025}, which raises the network's homogeneity degree".

4. Do not attribute the regularization-driven transition to McCracken, who hold L2 fixed at 1e-5. Support that half only with our own experiments.

5. Add one sentence noting that for ReLU networks the connection is interpretive, since our theorems cover product and power neurons.
